prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UK Independence Party Manifesto 2005 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core aim and rationale
- Leave the European Union to restore UK self-government, lawmaking and budget control. Repeal the European Communities Act, stop EU budget payments, and reassert UK legal primacy. Use a two-year transition to replace EU-derived laws and policies.

Economy and trade
- Maintain trade with EU via bilateral agreements (e.g., Swiss-style) and strengthen global links (Commonwealth, NAFTA, Far East). Regain an independent WTO seat.
- Deregulate extensively, prioritising relief for small businesses; scrap or amend EU-driven rules (e.g., Working Time Directive) unless a strong UK case exists.
- Budget: redirect the c.£1bn/year net EU payment to increase the state pension by £2/week. Temporarily borrow an extra £3bn/year for immediate tax cuts and priority spending, unconstrained by the EU Stability Pact.
- Tax: immediate steps—halve council tax for all households; scrap the 10% income tax band (paired with taking more low earners out of tax); reinstate dividend tax credits to rescue pensions; raise inheritance tax threshold to £500,000. Longer term—simplify radically: replace VAT with a wholesale sales tax; merge National Insurance with income tax; consider a low flat tax.

Health and welfare
- NHS: end central micromanagement; restore local control and matrons; scrap Strategic Health Authorities; extend GP hours; prioritise clinical judgement over targets; explore complementary private insurance models; remove EU limits on supplements/herbal medicines and doctors’ hours.
- Welfare: simplify and reduce means-testing to encourage work, saving and dignity; be sceptical of costly “active labour market” schemes.
- Pensions: immediate £2/week rise; reinstate dividend tax credits (+£5bn/year to funds); unfreeze expat pensions. Longer term, accept later retirement/more saving.

Education
- Schools: more autonomy; scrap SATs; headteachers to control exclusions; provision for excluded pupils; encourage specialisation and limited selection; abolish QCA; promote sport/trips; expand assisted places and consider vouchers/tax rebates for private education.
- Universities: review and defund low-standard courses; fully fund remaining courses; scrap top-up fees; restore maintenance grants; end student loans; charge EU students full international fees; expand high-quality technical education.

Law, immigration, and civil liberties
- Law and order: tougher, credible sentencing; empower lay magistrates; cut police paperwork; local accountability of chiefs; support homeowners’ self-defence; build prisons; resist EU “Corpus Juris.”
- Immigration: target near-zero net immigration; points-based work permits; treat EU and non-EU equally; tighten family rights; reinstate embarkation checks; “Britishness” and language tests; set UK asylum criteria with safe-third-country rule; faster removals; health checks.
- Civil liberties: repeal the Human Rights Act; oppose EU Charter; drop ID cards; roll back overreaching anti-terror laws; repeal the Hunting Act.

Agriculture, fisheries, energy, environment, transport
- Farming: leave CAP; restore deficiency-style supports; cut red tape; reopen small abattoirs; support green/organic and hill farming; consider Milk Marketing Board; strengthen biosecurity.
- Fisheries: leave CFP; reassert control of UK waters; enforce conservation (mesh sizes, fallow zones).
- Energy: halt wind turbine rollout; build new nuclear (fission) and back fusion R&D; support clean-coal.
- Environment: UK-set rules; prioritise waste reduction/recycling; protect countryside; ban GM crop planting until proven safe.
- Transport: invest in roads; review rail structure (possible reintegration of track and train); consider higher motorway limits; use speed cameras only at proven danger sites; resist EU transport mandates.

Governance and localism
- Uphold Commons, Lords, monarchy, common law; resist diluting Lords’ independence.
- Direct democracy: binding national or local referendums if 5% of voters petition within six months.
- Devolution: consider “English days” at Westminster; scrap English regional assemblies/quangos.
- Local government: more autonomy over planning; return business rates and property transfer duties to councils; cut politicised posts; prioritise core services; continue targeted regional aid post-EU.

Vision
- Smaller, more accountable government; fewer intrusive rules; stronger families and civic values; freer trade and enterprise leading to higher prosperity outside the EU.
